text:
maya: Quick sync — Q3 initiative: pick model-entry acceptance gates for the new multilingual model (costly but higher recall). Need product decision on SLA vs budget tradeoffs by EOD Friday.

lucas: recapped asks from sales: two enterprise customers want guaranteed pinning + 99.9% availability window for 1000 qps. They're willing to sign for a month of reserved capacity.

sasha: infra note: that model increases per-token GPU cost ~2.8x vs current medium model. If we guarantee pin + 1000 qps, it's multiple dedicated pools or very aggressive autoscale config.

ahmed: can we quantify latency impact? rough numbers from a quick run: 
```
benchmark: 1k-token avg request
- medium-model: p50 220ms, token-cost $0.0025
- multilingual-large: p50 340ms, token-cost $0.007
```
Those token-costs assume q4 kernels and dynamic batching.

jessica: customers care about tail latency (p99) too — they mentioned real-time chat. Any p99s?

ahmed: p99s for multilingual-large are ~1200ms under 1000rps unless we dedicate capacity. With dedicated pool and prewarm we can push p99 ~450ms but cost goes up ~3.6x.

lucas: product options to propose to customers: 1) Soft pin (best-effort) + cost-sharing credits 2) Hard pin with reserved capacity + premium 3) Canary pin with SLA ramp (30d) and auto-fallback to smaller model. Which is preferred?

sasha: engineering prefers 3) Canary pin with ramp and clear rollback policy. Minimizes long-term waste and gives us time to tune batching/kv-caching.

maya: sounds pragmatic. We need concrete acceptance gates for entry to catalog GA. Proposed gates: 
- Bench: p50 <= 400ms, p99 <= 600ms on dedicated small pool OR p50 <= 350ms, p99 <= 1200ms on soft-serve with documented fallback
- Cost: token unit cost delta <= 2.5x vs medium-model for soft-serve; <=3.5x for reserved contracts
- Reliability: canary (1% traffic) 14 days without regressions in top-5 customer prompts
- Customer opt-in: explicit opt-in + billing config for pinned customers

jessica: need to add monitoring gate: drift/quality alerts wired into Redwood Console, with automatic rollback on quality regression >5% relative to baseline.

maya: agree — add that. Also we should require a documented migration path for customers to fallback models (API-compatible).

catalog-bot: new entry created: MODEL-2026-MULTI-1, canary window flagged, owners: @sasha, @jessica.

lucas: timeline? if we accept these gates today, can engineering run a 14-day canary starting Mon and get a pass/fail report by month-end?

sasha: yes — need test datasets from sales for the top two customers, and an infra budget sign-off from finance.

maya: action items: 1) lucas collect customer test prompts (due Tue) 2) sasha schedule canary + infra estimate (due Wed) 3) jessica wire up quality alerts in Console (due Wed) 4) ahmed produce final bench report with p50/p99 and cost delta (due Thu)

lucas: I'll ping legal about SLA wording for reserved capacity.

maya: ok — if we hit the gates, we'll include this model in the Q3 catalog cadence as a "soft GA" with canary-first rollouts. If any gate fails, we default to option 3 rollback and a customer compensation plan. :thumbsup:
